topic: Quality Evidence Graph IPO Control Spec Kano Audit

kano_candidates.statement: IPO controlled Gate policy fixes DQ-first precedence, verdict priority, waiver limits, and conditional_go exit code 2.

evidence.summary: QEG must keep DQ precedence, verdict priority, and conditional_go exit code policy unambiguous for IPO-controlled use.

kano_candidates.statement: QEG verdict and human release approval are separate controls, and approval evidence must be independently auditable.

evidence.summary: QEG must not synthesize human release approval; approval evidence remains a distinct artifact with authority, role, package hash, and policy refs.

kano_candidates.statement: EvidencePackage must make release judgment reproducible through artifact hashes, phase, policy refs, manual evidence, approval evidence, and retention evidence.

evidence.summary: The more complete and hash-linked the evidence package is, the more release confidence and audit efficiency improve.

kano_candidates.statement: Retention, storage classification, tamper evidence, and silent overwrite detection are mandatory release control inputs.

evidence.summary: Silent overwrite and missing retention evidence directly break release traceability, especially for DQ-16.

kano_candidates.statement: The pre-implementation Gate combines manual-bb-test-harness and code-to-gate evidence while preserving IPO release No-Go separation.

evidence.summary: Combining manual-bb-test-harness with code-to-gate makes the requirement gate unusually strong and differentiating, while not replacing release approval.

known_biases: audit scope may miss undocumented requirements
implementation evidence can lag behind actual code state
